title: PayPal interview experience :
author: BALKARAN SINGH
body:
Getting an opportunity to interview with PayPal was a great learning experience for me. The process consisted of four interview rounds after the Online Assessment, with each round focusing on a different aspect of my technical and interpersonal skills.

1. Online Assessment (OA)

The process started with an Online Assessment, which primarily tested my DSA and problem-solving abilities. The questions required a good understanding of common data structures and algorithms along with the ability to arrive at an efficient solution within the given time.

For me, the OA was a good opportunity to revise the fundamentals and get comfortable with solving problems under time constraints.

2.Round 1 - DSA

The first interview round was focused primarily on Data Structures and Algorithms.

The interviewer gave me coding problems and discussed my approach, asking me to explain my thought process rather than simply jumping to the final solution. I had to think through different approaches, discuss their time and space complexities, and optimize where possible.

This round taught me the importance of communicating your thought process clearly while solving a problem. Even when you are unsure about the solution initially, explaining how you are approaching the problem can make the discussion much more productive.

3. Round 2 - Development, Projects, DSA & Core Fundamentals

The second round was more diverse. It covered development, projects, DSA, and core CS fundamentals.

A significant part of the discussion revolved around the projects I had mentioned on my resume. I was asked about the technologies I used, the reasoning behind my technical decisions, and how different parts of my projects worked.

Along with this, there were DSA questions and discussions around core computer science fundamentals.

This round reinforced one important lesson for me: don't put anything on your resume that you cannot explain. If you mention a technology, project, or concept, you should be comfortable discussing how it works and why you used it.

4. Round 3 — HR Round

The third round was an HR/behavioural round, with a combination of DSA and behavioural questions.

The behavioural questions focused on understanding how I approach different situations, communicate with others, deal with challenges, and learn from experiences.

There were also technical discussions, so it wasn't purely a conventional HR conversation.

I realized that technical skills are only one part of the interview. Being able to communicate clearly, explain your experiences honestly, and demonstrate a willingness to learn is equally important.

5. Round 4 — Hiring Manager Round

The final round was with the Hiring Manager.

This round focused on System Design and situational-based questions. The discussion was more open-ended and required me to think about how I would approach real-world situations and design problems.

Rather than looking for a single "perfect" answer, the discussion focused on my reasoning, decision-making, and ability to think through a problem.

One thing that particularly stayed with me from this round was the emphasis on curiosity and willingness to learn. It reminded me that interviews aren't always about knowing everything beforehand; they are also about demonstrating how you think and how you approach something you don't know.

My Internship Experience & Learnings

Once you get the internship, the learning doesn't stop. In fact, that's where another important part of the journey begins.

My biggest advice would be:

Be curious.

Don't limit yourself to just completing the project assigned to you. Try to understand why things are being done, how the system works, and how your work fits into the bigger picture.

Participate beyond your assigned project.

Internships are also a great opportunity to participate in extra-curricular activities, team events, challenges, presentations, and other initiatives happening within the organization.

These experiences help you learn things that you may not encounter while working solely on your assigned tasks.

Interact and build connections.

Talk to your teammates, mentors, managers, and other interns. Ask questions, learn about their experiences, and don't hesitate to initiate conversations.

The people you meet during an internship can become an important part of your professional journey.

Keep learning.

You don't need to know everything when you join. What matters is being willing to learn, ask questions, take feedback, and improve continuously.

For me, the biggest takeaway from the entire experience was that an internship isn't just about completing a project. It's about learning from the people around you, exploring new areas, building relationships, and making the most of the opportunity you're given.
